title: Sosulski et al. 2019 — Online Optimization of Stimulation Speed in an Auditory Brain-Computer Interface under Time Constraints
description: Auditory oddball (P300) EEG dataset from 13 healthy participants recorded with 31 channels at 1000 Hz. Target (1000 Hz) and non-target (500 Hz) tones were presented at stimulus onset asynchronies between 60 and 600 ms. The data support closed-loop optimization of individual stimulation speed in an auditory brain-computer interface, using Bayesian optimization and random search strategies to maximize classification performance of a regularized LDA classifier.
methods_description: Participants attended to target tones and ignored non-target tones while 31-channel EEG was recorded with a BrainProducts BrainAmp DC amplifier at 1000 Hz, with passive Ag/AgCl electrodes and a nose reference. The experiment had an optimization part and a validation part. In the optimization part, four strategies (AUC-ucb, AUC-rand, P300-ucb, P300-rand) each had 20 minutes to find the best SOA. In the validation part, the SOAs found by each strategy and a fixed 60 ms SOA were each tested in 20 trials. Features were mean amplitudes in five time intervals across channels, classified with shrinkage rLDA and 13-fold cross-validation.
